_about: Inputs to scripts/affected-rust-packages.py for the pull request tier (see .github/workflows/README.md). Every entry says why it exists in its `why` field.

repo_wide.name: install-wait scan and probe script tests
repo_wide.why: test_budget.py lists every tracked file (git ls-files) and fails when any file installs a chart without the install wait. A new file in any package can break it, so it runs on every pull request. It is the Python half of `cargo test -p alien-helm --test cni_probe`, run directly so no Rust build is needed.

repo_wide.name: release routing and metadata tests
repo_wide.why: These read the release workflows and the package manifests across the repository. They otherwise run only when a release starts.

repo_wide.name: selection script tests
repo_wide.why: The script decides what pull requests test, and this keeps every entry of this file pointing at something that exists. Cheap, and it reads the crates' manifests and test directories.

alien-core.why: schema/ holds the alien.toml schemas generated from alien-core's types, and the differential test resolves the checked-in fixtures into alien_core::Stack. A change to a core type makes them stale.

alien-core.filter: binary(runtime_metadata_round_trip) | binary(automatic_setup) | binary(event_state) | binary(observed_inventory) | binary(protected_stack_settings) | binary(quota_settings) | binary(stored_secret_presence)
alien-core.why: These send alien-core values through the client generated from the checked-in openapi.json. A core field the spec lacks is dropped, so a core change without a regenerated spec fails here.

alien-permissions.why: These test targets render or check permission sets from alien-permissions (four of them compile its iam_policy test harness with #[path]). A new action or permission set changes what they see.
The generator tests that render IAM from permission sets and compare the result with the boundary, the coverage rules and the grant parity.
The boundary document and boundary tests render the permission sets into CloudFormation.
The operator manifest tests render the permission sets into the chart's RBAC.

left_out.@alienplatform/bindings: Its tests load the native addon, which needs a Rust build of alien-bindings-node (minutes). The nightly and release runs test it.

@alienplatform/core.why: packages/core/src/__tests__/platform-binding-serialization.test.ts imports the generated platform client by relative path, and core's generated schemas come from the OpenAPI specs.

@alienplatform/permissions.why: packages/permissions/test.mjs reads the operation catalog in crates/alien-permissions and runs its operation-permission-compiler, so a change to the crate changes what the package tests check.

every_package_inputs.why: The lockfile, the workspace list and the root manifest decide which dependencies every package installs, so a change to any of them selects every test package.
